newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gonzalez says Serbian opposition won elections.
newsitem.headline: Gonzalez says Serbian opposition won elections.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez said on Friday he had come to the conclusion that the opposition Zajedno coalition had won local elections in 13 municipalities as well as nine municipalities in Belgrade.

In a statement issued to the leadership of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), Gonzalez also called on the OSCE to issue an "urgent appeal" to authorities and political forces in Yugoslavia "comply with the will exppressed at the polls by the citizens."
Gonzalez, who headed a fact-finding mission on behalf of the OSCE, made his report available shortly before a news conference.
He said the "authorities as well as all political forces in the federal republic of Yugoslavia should accept the results of the local elections of November 17."

Despite some criticism he had heard on the functioning of the Serbian electoral system, Gonzalez said the system had "made it possible for the majority will of the citizens of the federal republic of Yugoslavia to be reflected."

Gonzalez also said the results of the election in other municipalities were not in doubt, nor the fact that taken together the coalition parties around Milosovic's ruling socialist party "won the majority of the votes in the elections."
The statement provided the following list of municipalities where Gonzalez said the Zajedno coalition won the elections:
Pirot, Kraljevo, Uzice, Smederevska Pallanka, Vrasac, Soko Banja, Kraguejevac, Pancevo, Jagodina, Nis, Zrenjanin, Lapovo, Sabac and the nine municipalities of Belgrade.
